label: Aristotle, Metaphysics IX.3, 1046b29-32: The Megarian thesis: a thing is able only when it is…
interpretation: Aristotle reports that some, such as the Megarians, say a thing is able only when it is acting (ὅταν ἐνεργῇ μόνον δύνασθαι), as the one not building is not able to build. Read with the Θ.6 primitive CanBe: whatever is able to be r is actually r. Aristotle generalizes it to the inanimate and to perception (1047a4-10); the formalization keeps the general form. Aristotle says these views make potency and act the same (1047a19-20).
